request.questionText: Pokémon is a Japanese media franchise consisting of a universe in which humans co-exist with “pocket monsters”, or Pokémon. These creatures --- most inspired by real-world animals or mythical folklore --- are a large variety of species endowed with special powers. The pokemon data frame includes information on 949 Pokémon, including the following features: name -- name of Pokémon height -- in meters experience -- base experience points stamina -- hit points, measure for health attack -- attack points defense -- defense points psychic -- no/yes indicator for whether type is psychic The franchise's primary target audience is children aged 5 to 12, but it is known to attract people of all ages. Imagine that you are a Pokémon fanatic, hoping to use insights from data to gain an edge in battles. Fit a linear model to predict attack points in terms of: height psychic the interaction between height and psychic Fill in the blanks below to provide accurate interpretations of the results of this model: We are 95% confident that a one-meter increase in height for a non-psychic Pokémon is associated with [ Select ] ["a decrease", "an increase"] of at most approximately [ Select ] ["11", "18", "12", "9", "28"] attack points. A non-psychic Pokémon is expected with 95% confidence to have at least approximately 7 attack points more than a psychic Pokémon of the same height, on average. For psychic Pokémon, each additional meter in height is associated with [ Select ] ["an increase", "a decrease"] of approximately [ Select ] ["9", "2", "15", "19", "11"] attack points. The relationship between attack points and height for psychic Pokémon [ Select ] ["is significantly different", "is not significantly different"] than that of non-psychic Pokémon, with 95% confidence.
